comparisons.peer_summary: The firm may modify terms for borrowers in financial difficulty, primarily via term extensions; modified loans were mostly performing, with negligible defaults in 2024 and ~$100 million charged off in 2023 from previously modified loans.
comparisons.comparison: The target disclosure (BAC) focuses specifically on the volume of commitments to lend to borrowers with modified loans ($1.3 billion). GS discusses the policy and outcomes of these modifications, noting that modified loans were primarily term extensions and that defaults after modification were not material in 2024. Unlike BAC, GS does not provide a specific aggregate dollar figure for unfunded commitments to these modified borrowers, instead focusing on the nature of the modifications (term extensions) and performance (negligible defaults).

sentences.text: For 2024 and 2023, the Corporation had commitments to lend $1.3 billion and $1.2 billion to commercial borrowers experiencing financial difficulty whose loans were modified during the period.
The firm may modify the terms of a loan agreement for a borrower experiencing financial difficulty.

• During 2024, loans that defaulted after being modified were not material. During 2023, the firm charged off approximately $100 million of loans that had defaulted after being modified. Substantially all of the remaining modified loans were performing in accordance with the modified contractual terms as of both December 2024 and December 2023.

comparisons.peer_summary: As of December 31, 2024 and 2023, there were no additional commitments to lend to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty whose loans had been modified as financial distress modifications (FDMs).
comparisons.comparison: Both disclosures address commitments to lend to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty with modified loans, but report opposite outcomes. BAC reports $1.3 billion in such commitments for 2024. In contrast, JPM states that as of December 31, 2024 and 2023, there were 'no additional commitments to lend to borrowers experiencing financial difficulty whose loans have been modified as FDMs.' This highlights a significant difference in the level of new lending exposure to this specific distressed population between the two firms.
